1	---
2	name: caveman
3	description: >
4	  Ultra-compressed communication mode that cuts output tokens while keeping
5	  technical accuracy. Levels: lite, full, ultra and the wenyan variants. Use for
6	  /caveman, "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "be brief" or "less tokens".
7	---
8	
9	Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.
10	
11	## Persistence
12	
13	Default style for this whole session, every response, until user say "stop caveman" or "normal mode". Keep terse on long sessions no filler drift.
14	
15	Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra|wenyan-lite|wenyan-full|wenyan-ultra|off`.
16	
17	## Rules
18	
19	Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.
20	
21	Never drop not/never/no/only/except flip meaning worse than any token saved. Numbers, units exact.
22	
23	Never ADD word to sound caveman. Compression only style never grow output. No inserted pronoun or copula to fake broken grammar: "when it not" cost one token more than "when not" and say same thing. Keep correct verb form when correct form cost same "sees" one token, "see" one token, so mangle buy nothing and read worse. Same rule as abbreviations and arrows: if caveman phrasing not shorter than plain phrasing, use plain.
24	
25	Clarity register: mix ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English into caveman, always. One idea per sentence. Sentence short, target 20 words max. Active voice. Present tense where true. One word one meaning: same term for same thing every time, no synonym rotation. Instruction = imperative: "Run X", not "X should be run". Noun cluster 3 words max. Pronoun only with one clear referent, else repeat noun. Caveman cut filler; STE keep what make meaning unambiguous. Conflict between them → clarity win.
26	
27	Tool calls: fire direct. No preamble, plan, or progress note before or between calls. After result: next call direct or final answer never announce next call. Text before call only to clarify, warn security/irreversible, or resolve ambiguity.
28	
29	Follow explicit reply-language instructions from the user or project. Otherwise preserve the user's dominant language. Never switch because of example text or multilingual context elsewhere. p='bot.mjs'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("export async function checkSend({ user, message, now } = {}) {\n  try {\n","export async function checkSend(input) {\n  try {\n    const { user, message, now } = input ?? {};\n")

text:
`bot.mjs` is written and exports `checkSend`. It sends nothing and never reads the clock. I ran it against 26 cases (all pass) plus six malformed inputs. One of those, `null`, made it throw. I fixed that, and now none of them throw. The test script is in `/tmp/gt/t.mjs`, outside the project.

**Rules, checked in this order.** Each hold has its own identifier:

| `rule` | Holds the text when |
|---|---|
| `invalid-user` | `user` is missing or not an object. |
| `opted-out` | `optedOutAt` has any value. This holds transactional texts too, so a login code is also held after STOP. |
| `invalid-message` | The text is missing, not a string, or blank. |
| `no-consent` | The text is marketing and `optedIn` is not exactly `true`. |
| `missing-opt-out` | The text is marketing and has no "Reply STOP to opt out" style wording. |
| `invalid-time` | The text is marketing and `now` is not a valid Date. |
| `unknown-time-zone` | The text is marketing and `timeZone` is missing or not a real zone. |
| `quiet-hours` | The text is marketing and the customer's local time is before 08:00 or at/after 21:00. |

**Calls I made, which you may want to change:**
- **Marketing definition:** any `kind` other than exactly `"transactional"` is treated as marketing, as you defined it.
- **Promotional wording:** a "transactional" text that contains words like "% off", "sale" or "use code" is also treated as marketing. The FCC treats a shipping notice with a coupon in it as a sales text. The word list is rough, so it may miss some promotions and catch some plain notices.
- **Transactional texts:** they skip the `optedIn`, time-zone and quiet-hours checks. A login code at 3am goes out even if the time zone is missing. They are only held for `opted-out`, blank text or a missing user.
- **Opt-out wording:** I added the `missing-opt-out` check from the CTIA guidance. I can't check for your business name in the text, so that is not covered.
- **Time-zone fallback:** when `timeZone` is missing or invalid, marketing is held rather than guessed. No local window works for the US, India and Japan at once. Customers with no time zone get no marketing until their profile is fixed. A valid but wrong zone can't be detected.
- **Opt-out vs. opt-in:** a set `optedOutAt` wins even if `optedIn` is `true`, since the function can't tell which came later. A customer who re-subscribes needs `optedOutAt` cleared on your side.

**Not covered:**
- The National Do Not Call list, because it needs outside data.
- Stricter state quiet hours, such as Florida's 8am–8pm. Say if you want the window narrowed to 8am–8pm.
